capabilities.claim: Reads the version a Luraph banner comment names and maps it to a profiled generation.
capabilities.proves: The banner text is parsed as written, versions are mapped to the generation whose period they fall in, versions outside the profile are not mapped, and the result is capped at 0.7 confidence with a caveat.
capabilities.doesNotProve: That the banner is true. A banner is a comment: anyone can add, edit or remove one. Nothing is claimed about reconstruction.

checks.name: a forged banner is reported as claimed, not as established

capabilities.claim: Narrows the Luraph generation a source script was written for from the macros it uses.
capabilities.proves: For every generation, the macros the vendor SDK defines for it give a candidate set that includes it; macros introduced later narrow the set; a macro no generation defines gives none.
capabilities.doesNotProve: That a script using those macros has been, or will be, protected by that generation, or that the service rejects macros the SDK omits. It applies to unprotected source scripts only: protected output no longer contains macros. Nothing is claimed about reconstruction.

checks.name: v13-era: its own 7 macros include v13-era among the candidates
v14: its own 11 macros include v14 among the candidates
v15: its own 12 macros include v15 among the candidates
v15.1: its own 14 macros include v15.1 among the candidates
macros first seen in v15.1 (LPH_ASSUME, LPH_OPAQUE) narrow to v15.1 alone
a macro no generation defines gives no candidate and low confidence
a script with no macros is not said to be Luraph

capabilities.claim: No profile can say "supported" without real or authorised evidence.
capabilities.proves: Every shipped profile validates, no commercial profile is above identification-only, and hand-made profiles that over-claim are rejected by the validator.
capabilities.doesNotProve: That the evidence the gates ask for is good: it proves the gates are enforced.

checks.name: a commercial version cannot be marked real-output-verified
authorised-sample status without pairs is rejected

capabilities.claim: Decides whether a reconstruction behaves like its original by running both on a reference Lua runtime.
capabilities.proves: Equal programs are reported identical, a changed program is reported different (a check that cannot fail would prove nothing), and a program that prints nothing is reported inconclusive.
capabilities.doesNotProve: Behaviour on inputs the program was not run with, or on Luau (not installed here).

capabilities.claim: Recognises output of Prometheus (signature).
capabilities.proves: On a spread sample of 6 fixtures made by the real tool, the detector names prometheus with confidence of at least 0.5 on at least 80%.
capabilities.doesNotProve: Recognition on output made with other settings, other versions, or after further processing.

capabilities.claim: Reconstructs output of Prometheus so that it behaves like the protected script.
capabilities.proves: On a spread sample of 6 real-tool fixtures, at least 4 are decided on a reference runtime and at least 70% of those behave identically to the original program.
capabilities.doesNotProve: Coverage of every setting or program. The full result and its interval are in the profile; this is a re-measurement of a sample.
